subject: MedLink: security add-on economics and approval pathway
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Graves <tom.graves@medlink.ai>, procurement@medlink.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: MedLink: security add-on economics and approval pathway

Tom / MedLink procurement team — thanks again for the time this morning. As promised, I wanted to summarize the pricing options we discussed for the compliance/security bundle (audit logs, KMS/HSM seats, and EU residency option) and outline the quickest approval path so you can get the pilot moving next week.

Summary of options (short):
- Pilot bundle (90-day): audit log tier A (30 days retention), 2 HSM seats, soft residency routing to EU region — one-time pilot credit applied. Proposed list price = $18,000 for pilot (one-time), we offered a 20% pilot concession.
- Annual committed bundle: audit log tier B (90 days retention), 4 HSM seats, guaranteed EU data residency w/ SLA for residency routing. Annual list recurring = $220k. We proposed a blended compliance credit of 12% if they commit 12 months.
- Transition/residency fee: one-time setup for on-prem routing / network proofing = $15k (amortize over 6 months or invoice upfront).

Key ask for procurement: confirm whether MedLink will sign the SOW with the pilot concession (DocuSign link below) or whether procurement needs an invoice-first PoO. If invoice-first, we can convert the pilot credit into a net credit applied on the first invoice.

Notes / justification for pricing structure:
- The 20% pilot concession is limited to a single account pilot and is tied to an explicit demo + success criteria (latency < 100ms 95th pct for routed EU requests).
- The annual blended credit requires a 12-month commit for consistent routing capacity; the credit is not combinable with channel rebates or marketplace promos.

Attached: MedLink_Compliance_Pricing_worksheet_v1.xlsx (line-item breakout), draft SOW for residency (SOW_data_residency_draft.pdf).

DocuSign link (pilot SOW): https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/DocuSign-Envelope-123abc
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Next steps I recommend:
1) Procurement to confirm preferred billing (invoice-first vs DocuSign).
2) If DocuSign: MedLink signs pilot SOW, we provision pilot credits and route to EU region.
3) After 30 days of pilot success, move to an ARR order with the 12% blended credit if they commit.

If anyone on our team has concerns about the concession levels or the residency SLA wording, flag here so I can adjust before sending the DocuSign.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of GTM Finance, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0107

Subject: Re: MedLink: security add-on economics and approval pathway

Naomi — thanks for the recap and the spreadsheet. A couple of clarifying Qs from our procurement lead: 1) for the pilot concession, can the 20% be reflected as a refundable prepay in case we fail the success criteria (i.e., we get refunded unused portion)? 2) the residency SLA has to include a rollback plan to US routing during outages — do you have language for that in the SOW?

Procurement also wants to know if we can phase the HSM seat ramp (start with 1 seat on day 1, add a second at go/no-go) and have the pricing reflect seat ramping instead of a single up-front line item.

We are leaning to DocuSign for speed but will confirm once procurement completes the PO checklist.

— Tom

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: MedLink: security add-on economics and approval pathway

Naomi — quick internal note before we respond to Tom.

1) Refundable prepay: I don't love refundable prepay for pilots — administratively messy and sets a precedent. Recommend: convert refundable prepay ask to a holdback credit in the SOW. If they fail success criteria we apply a prorated credit back to their account rather than issuing refunds.
2) HSM seat ramp: totally fine to price as ramping: $3,500/month per HSM seat prorated, ramp schedule in SOW. Keep the pilot bundle as '2 seat equivalent' in pricing worksheet so sales math stays simple, but include a line that allows seat ramping with prorated invoicing.
3) Residency rollback language: Rafael, can you draft a short rollback clause that preserves SLA credits if we have to route back to US for <72 hours and codifies a notification window?

Also — we should avoid a single-use 20% concession that becomes expectation. Suggest moving from 20% pilot concession to a structured pilot credit: 15% base pilot credit + a $5k P0 performance accelerator credit (paid only if they achieve the stated latency objective and provide the success metrics). This keeps us protected yet gives them upside.

If Laura or Rafael disagree, shout now. I can incorporate into the SOW and pricing worksheet.

-ben
Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
ben.carter@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:18:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: MedLink: security add-on economics and approval pathway

Ben — drafting rollback/regional-fallback clause now. High-level draft for internal review: 

"If Redwood must temporarily reroute traffic originating from EU to US data centers due to infrastructure incidents or third-party provider outages, Redwood will: (a) notify MedLink within 60 minutes of detection, (b) provide a technical incident report within 48 hours, and (c) apply a pro-rated SLA credit for any residency-related breaches beyond the 72-hour soft window. If the failover is expected to exceed 7 days, Redwood will work with MedLink on a temporary residency remediation plan at agreed costs."

I recommend the 72-hour soft window (no credit) and pro-rated credits after that — matches our current incident tolerance and gives them runway to recover. For the SOW I'll add a clause that allows a one-time exception for major cloud provider outages.

Also appended a seat-ramping schedule snippet for SOW pricing: 1st HSM seat active day 1 at $3,500/mo, 2nd seat added on go/no-go at prorated amount for that month, subsequent seats monthly billed.

I'll update the worksheet and push a redlined SOW with these changes for Naomi to review before we send to MedLink.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Looping in quick approval from me: I support Ben's approach (15% base + $5k performance accelerator) instead of 20% upfront. Procurement teams like clear success incentives and it aligns CS + Sales. One operational ask: if we convert refundable prepay to a holdback credit, ensure finance has a clear aging bucket so it doesn't sit in unallocated credits for >90 days. Naomi, Rafael — can you add an explicit expiry on credits (90 days post-pilot) in the SOW?

If all good I'll greenlight sending the updated SOW to Tom with the DocuSign link and the seat-ramping language.

Naomi / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the updated approach. Procurement reviewed the revised terms and prefers the holdback-credit approach rather than refundable prepay — that should be fine. They also like the 15% base + $5k accelerator structure (gives them an incentive model for success metrics).

Two final asks before we click DocuSign: 1) please add an explicit credit-expiry clause for pilot credits (procurement requests 90 days max), and 2) confirm the rollback/notification window as Rafael proposed (60-minute notice, 72-hour soft window). If we can get those two items explicitly called out in the redline SOW, we will move to signature today.

We appreciate the flexibility — looking forward to getting the pilot started next week.
